h1:
Koh Phangan Specialty Coffee
Local Roasters & Chill Sea-View Work Cafes
intro: Koh Phangan isn't only parties and beaches anymore — it's quietly turned into a coffee town for remote workers. There are roasters who roast their own beans on the island, cool air-conditioned cafes where you can park a laptop all day, and sea-view spots for an afternoon brain break. We've picked the places that are actually open right now, and flagged which ones are good for getting work done versus just hanging out.

blocks.html: Lately Koh Phangan has drawn a lot more long-stay remote workers, especially around Srithanu, the island's yoga and wellness hub. One nice side effect: good coffee shops keep popping up, many of them roasting their own beans from northern Thai coffee, and some running as all-day brunch spots you can work from for hours. We've grouped the cafes by zone so it's easy to picture, because hopping between zones by scooter takes a while on Koh Phangan and some roads get seriously steep.

blocks.text: Roasters and specialty cafes worth trying

blocks.html: These are the cafes we picked from real reviews and places still open as of now, ordered from spots best for long work sessions down to ones for a quick single cup. Prices are rough ranges and may shift with the season and menu.

items.name: Bubba's Roastery (Haad Yao / Thong Sala / Ban Tai)
items.blurb: The island's real roaster — they roast their own beans from northern Thai coffee and supply other cafes across Phangan, Samui and Koh Tao. The Haad Yao branch is the main roastery, while Thong Sala and Ban Tai are all-day brunch cafes with long communal tables, cold air-con and a garden corner. A proper place to settle in and work.
items.meta: Open all day · beans roasted on the island · work-friendly

items.name: Indigo Specialty Coffee & Bakery (Thong Sala / Hin Kong)
items.blurb: A tropical-style specialty cafe in indigo-blue tones with its own bakery, wide tables, plenty of plugs and cold air-con, open roughly morning to evening. There are vegan options too. Remote workers love settling in here for the long haul thanks to the calm vibe and comfy seating.

items.name: Balance Specialty Coffee (near Thong Sala)
items.blurb: A small cafe tucked in greenery near Thong Sala, with Australian-style brewing — the flat white and cappuccino are done well. There's an outdoor terrace and an air-conditioned room, plus a leafy, quiet setting that's great for focusing on work in the morning.

items.name: Dots Coffee (near Thong Sala pier)
items.blurb: A retro-modern cafe with fast Wi-Fi, right by Thong Sala pier — handy for working or killing time while you wait for a boat. It does breakfast, and it's a spot remote workers drop by often.
items.meta: Near the pier · fast Wi-Fi · breakfast served

items.name: Footprint Cafe (Srithanu, lakeside)
items.blurb: A lakeside cafe in the Srithanu area with a calm vibe and water views — good for a relaxed brain break or some light morning work. It sits right in the island's yoga district, so it's an easy walk on to a healthy meal afterwards.
items.meta: Srithanu · lake view · calm and quiet

items.name: What's Cup! (Haad Yao, clifftop)
items.blurb: A coffee shop on the cliff above Haad Yao with a well-pulled espresso and cold-pressed juices. The draw is the sea view and the beach below — better for a single cup in the breeze than digging in for a long work day, since seating is limited.

items.name: Hundred Islands Coffee Bar (Thong Sala)
items.blurb: A modern-toned coffee bar with friendly staff, a chill vibe and usable Wi-Fi — good for a short work session or a casual work catch-up. It's right in Thong Sala town, so finding food nearby is easy.

items.name: Sticky Island Cafe (central island)
items.blurb: An airy, light-filled cafe with a menu leaning toward healthy food — great if you want to work somewhere bright and easy on the eyes. The coffee is solid, and it's another spot the wellness crowd drops by.

items.name: Nira's Home Bakery (central island)
items.blurb: A spacious, air-conditioned bakery where it's easy to focus, with an Asian–European fusion menu and fresh-baked goods. Good if you want both coffee and a real meal in one place — popular with remote workers.

items.name: Eat.Co (Srithanu)
items.blurb: A fully vegan cafe in Srithanu with comfy seating — chairs, sofas and floor cushions — plus cacao shots. A good fit for the wellness crowd who want to work quietly in the yoga district.

blocks.title: Picking a cafe by zone
blocks.html: Thong Sala = lots of cafes, near the pier and convenience stores, good for settling in to work · Haad Yao = sea views and Bubba's roastery · Srithanu = wellness and yoga, quiet lakeside cafes · Before riding across zones, check the distance on Google Maps first — some roads are steep and narrow, so ride slow.

blocks.text: Sea-view cafes for a brain break

blocks.html: Work all day and you need somewhere to rest your eyes. These spots stand out more for the view than for long work sessions — drop by for a single cup and some afternoon sea breeze.

items.name: What's Cup! Haad Yao
items.blurb: On the cliff above Haad Yao, with coffee and a wide sea view — great in the late afternoon before sunset. Seating is limited, so come early or in the late afternoon to grab a good spot.

items.name: Footprint Cafe Srithanu
items.blurb: Lakeside in the Srithanu area, with quiet water views — perfect for a brain break after a yoga class, or a morning coffee before you start work.

items.name: Sand & Tan Haad Rin
items.blurb: A spot on Haad Rin where you really can drink coffee right by the sea. Prices run higher than in-town cafes because of the beachfront location, so it's more for chilling than for working.

blocks.text: Working smoothly on the island — what to know

items: Cafe Wi-Fi often beats your accommodation — internet on the island isn't as stable as in big cities, so if you have important work, bring a backup mobile data SIM.
Check opening hours before you go — some cafes close early in low season or have irregular days off. Check their page or Google Maps before you leave your accommodation.
Watch your valuables — don't leave a laptop or phone on the table when you step to the restroom, especially at open-air seafront cafes.
Mind the steep roads on a scooter — many roads on the island are steep and get slippery in the rain. Always wear a helmet, ride slow, and avoid riding remote roads at night.
Allow time to cross zones — getting from Thong Sala to Haad Rin or Haad Yao takes a while. Planning to work within one zone per day is a lot less tiring.

blocks.text: A 2-day cafe-hopping trip on Koh Phangan

blocks.html: If you want to sample coffee and get some work done at the same time, here's a route that doesn't ride too far each day — split by zone so you're not crossing the island over and over.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Thong Sala zone — settle in and work

items.activity: Start the morning at Bubba's Coffee Thong Sala
items.note: Order brunch with an espresso and grab a long table to work the morning while your head's still fresh.

items.activity: Lunch break in Thong Sala town
items.note: Easy to find food stalls around the market, all close by.

items.activity: Move to Indigo Specialty Coffee to keep working
items.note: Cold air-con and plenty of plugs — good for a long focused afternoon.

items.activity: Wrap up, swing by the Thong Sala evening market
items.note: On Saturdays there's a walking street with lots of food.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Haad Yao–Srithanu zone — chill by the sea

items.activity: Stop by Bubba's Roastery Haad Yao
items.note: Coffee from the main roastery — you can buy fresh-roasted beans to take home.

items.activity: Head up to What's Cup! for the clifftop sea view
items.note: Seating is limited — have a single cup in the breeze and move on.

items.activity: Down to Srithanu for a healthy meal + Eat.Co
items.note: The yoga district, with several vegan cafes and healthy spots.

items.activity: Finish at Footprint Cafe by the lake
items.note: Sip a coffee and watch the sun drop over the water in peace.

faq.q: Does Koh Phangan have specialty coffee shops that roast their own beans?
faq.a: Yes — Bubba's Roastery is the island's main roaster, roasting its own beans from northern Thai coffee. It has branches at Haad Yao (the main roastery), Thong Sala and Ban Tai, and also supplies beans to other cafes across Phangan, Samui and Koh Tao.

faq.q: Which cafes are best for long work sessions on Koh Phangan?
faq.a: Indigo Specialty Coffee in Thong Sala stands out for wide tables, plenty of plugs and cold air-con. Bubba's in Thong Sala has long communal tables, and Dots Coffee near the pier has fast Wi-Fi — all good for settling in to work the whole day.

faq.q: How much does coffee cost on Koh Phangan?
faq.a: Most cappuccinos run around ฿70–100. In-town cafes in Srithanu and Thong Sala tend to be cheaper, while beachfront spots like those on Haad Rin can climb to around ฿120 because of the seaside location.

faq.q: Is the Wi-Fi on Koh Phangan good enough to work on?
faq.a: Plenty of cafes have decent Wi-Fi, but the island's internet overall isn't as stable as in big cities. If you have important work or online meetings, bring a backup mobile data SIM as well.

faq.q: Which cafe zone suits remote workers best?
faq.a: Thong Sala is good for settling in to work — lots of cafes, near the pier and convenience stores. Srithanu suits the wellness and yoga crowd, with quiet lakeside cafes. If you want sea views, head to the Haad Yao zone.
